source_text: Some Islamic scholars, particularly from the Shafi'i and Hanbali schools of jurisprudence, have endorsed mild forms of female genital modification, classifying Type Ia—typically involving a symbolic prick or removal of the prepuce—as sunnah (recommended) or makrumah (honorable) to promote modesty and control desire, drawing on hadiths such as the narration attributed to Umm Atiyyah where the Prophet Muhammad reportedly advised a minor procedure on girls. [36]
